tn_lake_nickajack_deep_water_soloing.blurb: A limestone wall of roughly fifty feet rising straight from Nickajack Lake near Guild, close to the Interstate 24 bridge. It is a swimsuit-and-shoes kind of place: tufas and small roofs on vertical to slightly overhanging rock, with the lake below to catch a fall. The fourteen lines are a mix of top-rope and sport, running from easy 5.6 and 5.7 steps through a solid cluster of 5.10s up to a few 5.11 and 5.12 and one 5.13 test piece. Water depth below the wall is only estimated, so check it yourself, and the lake level changes with dam releases. Go with a partner, and wear flotation.

tn_frumundathunda_boulder.blurb: A single well-known boulder in the Jungle Gym part of Stone Fort (Little Rock City), a wooded boulder park outside Chattanooga. Thirteen problems are packed onto it, spanning one easy line in the V1 range, a good middle band from V3 to V6, and a couple of real tests at V8 and V10. The nearby gully holds a small stream, and the surrounding blocks include occasional pebble-studded rock. It makes a worthwhile stop for a climber working through the V4 and V5 grades, with a pad and a spotter on the taller moves.

tn_dihedrals_the.blurb: A sandstone wall in the Falls area of Foster Falls, near Jasper, in the Cumberland Plateau country west of Chattanooga. Mostly face climbing on bolts, with two traditional lines among thirteen routes. It is a friendlier stretch of the cliff than much of Foster Falls: a few routes sit at 5.8 and 5.9, the bulk lie between 5.9 and 5.11, and a handful top out at 5.12 and 5.13 for hard-pushing sport climbers. Plenty of stars among them, so it often draws a queue on good days. Foster Falls itself can be climbed nearly year-round.

tn_m_northwest_buttress.blurb: A trad-only buttress in the Sunset South section of Sunset Rock, on Lookout Mountain above Chattanooga. All thirteen routes are protected by your own gear and sit in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a good number at 5.10, so it suits leaders stepping up from moderate trad. The wall begins with a bulging overhang beside the trail, lays back to easier ground, then steepens into a pale headwall; a few lines take two pitches. The crag faces west and stays shaded well into the afternoon, which makes it a pleasant summer choice and a cool one in winter.
